subject: microbiology
title: Staphylococcal Enterotoxin Food Poisoning, Scalded Skin Syndrome and MRSA

steps.tx: Staphylococcal **enterotoxins** (A to E and successors) are heat stable superantigens preformed in food (creams, custards, processed meats, potato salads handled and left warm): reheating kills bacteria but toxin survives, vomiting erupts within one to six hours of eating, cramps and sometimes diarrhoea follow, fever absent, recovery inside a day. The food handler's colonised hands are the usual kitchen source.
steps.say: Toxin already in the food, vomiting within hours, gone by tomorrow: reheating cannot save it.

left.title: Food poisoning portrait
points: Vomiting dominant, cramps, low or no fever
Groups sharing one dish outbreak pattern

right.title: Food and toxin facts
points: Salt and sugar tolerant growth in custards and meats
Handler nasal and skin carriage seeds food

steps.tx: **Scalded skin syndrome** (staphylococcal) sends exfoliative toxins A and B (serine proteases splitting desmoglein 1) through blood from a trivial focus to skin everywhere, separating epidermis superficially (Nikolsky positive) in infants and children, sparing mucosa (the split is above it), healing without scars as superficial wounds do, contrasting TEN where full thickness and mucosa die.
steps.say: Toxin splits skin at desmoglein 1 from a distant focus; mucosa spared divides it from TEN.

left.title: SSSS portrait
points: Infants and young children (renal toxin clearance immature)
Tender erythema, bullae, sheet like peeling
Culture the focus (nose, umbilicus), skin sterile of bacteria

right.title: SSSS versus TEN
points: Prognosis far kinder in SSSS children

steps.tx: **MRSA** from the genetics module owns epidemiology: hospital associated lineages in devices and wounds, community lineages (PVL often) in boils and pneumonia, livestock associated niches, colonisation screening in high risk admissions, isolation and contact precautions, decolonisation suppressing rather than erasing. Its name (methicillin) commemorates an antibiotic most laboratories no longer test.
steps.say: MRSA is a resistance phenotype with three epidemiologies: hospital, community and livestock.

left.title: MRSA worlds
points: Community: skin sepsis in healthy, PVL kin
Screening nares (plus throat, perineum by policy)

right.title: MRSA control
points: Contact precautions and single rooms by risk
Decolonisation before elective high risk surgery

steps.tx: **Impetigo and ecthyma** return briefly because aureus shares them with Streptococcus pyogenes: honey crusted lesions (either), bullous impetigo by exfoliative toxin (aureus signature), ecthyma ulcerating deeper (streptococcal leaning), treated by extent (topical mupirocin limited, oral agents widespread) with local resistance patterns consulted.
steps.say: Honey crusts have two authors; bullae sign the staphylococcal one.

left.title: Impetigo forms
points: Non bullous: aureus and pyogenes mixed
Contagious in schools and contact sports
Post streptococcal GN follows skin strains (pyogenes)

right.title: Treatment logic
points: Limited: topical mupirocin or retapamulin geography

steps.tx: **Toxin food poisoning differential** sharpens outbreak interviews: Bacillus cereus emetic (fried rice, similar hours), Clostridium perfringens (8 to 16 hours diarrhoea dominant), chemical and heavy metal (minutes), viral gastroenteritis (longer, fever), each incubation and symptom vote narrowing the food diary. Incubation period is the first laboratory test an outbreak takes.
steps.say: Ask when symptoms started before what was eaten; the clock names the toxin.

left.title: Short incubation vomiting
points: B cereus emetic 0.5 to 6 hours (fried rice)

steps.tx: **Outbreak investigation** for staphylococcal food poisoning cultures leftover food and handler lesions, enterotoxin assays in food by reference laboratories, and stool cultures that mostly miss the preformed point. Attack rates by dish, incubation medians and food handling timelines convict the custard before any isolate types.
steps.say: Interview the menu and the clock; the organism may have left only its toxin behind.

nodes.label: Cases listed with foods and onset times

steps.tx: **Mupirocin resistance and decolonisation failure** follow use: low level (MIC creep) and high level (plasmid mupA) resistance rise where decolonisation is mass applied, chlorhexidine tolerance genes (qac) tracked, protocols time limited and targeted. Eradication claims should be read as suppression windows around surgery and outbreaks.
steps.say: Decolonisation is a timed suppression, not a sterilised nose forever.

left.title: Decolonisation regimen
points: Nasal mupirocin twice daily five days
Targeted: pre surgical, ICU, outbreak cohorts

right.title: Failure modes
points: Non adherence to body wash days

steps.tx: **Staphylococcal carriage in food handlers and healthcare** closes the loop between lessons: exclusion of handlers with draining lesions from food preparation (not asymptomatic carriage alone), healthcare outbreak policies screening staff epidemiologically, and the principle that toxin diseases are prevented at colonisation and temperature, not treated at the table.
steps.say: Exclude draining lesions, refrigerate promptly; toxin prevention happens before the meal.

right.title: Care setting
points: Staff screening only by outbreak evidence
